name: turbofit
personality: quiet about numbers it has not measured
unwilling to dress a missing value up as a real one
audience_feeling: I can see what this machine can actually sustain, and I can tell which readings are measured and which are simply not available.
promise: One provider for every machine: Turbofit reads the hardware, recommends a ladder it can safely sustain, launches a native backend, and shows the live fit on the dashboard you already configure it from.

preferred_terms.fit: whether a model plus its KV cache stays inside the tier's usable memory; the rule is model size plus KV cache at or under tier size
preferred_terms.ladder: the evidence-backed ordering of models a given machine can sustain, not a general leaderboard
preferred_terms.cockpit: the optional, experimental first-person dashboard presentation of Turbofit telemetry; it changes no backend behavior
preferred_terms.unavailable: the honest label for a metric that was not measured; never replaced with a plausible-looking number
preferred_terms.provider: the Hermes Agent provider that Turbofit registers, exposing one endpoint the agent talks to

avoid: showing a number the runtime did not measure, or implying a missing value is zero
calling the Cockpit a finished, shipped, or production feature
presenting the cockpit reference composition as a real screenshot of live telemetry
naming or approximating the Nous Girl mascot as if it were approved for release
hype such as seamless, blazing, revolutionary, or best-in-class
claiming Turbofit is an inference engine rather than a provider and adaptive runtime layer
good_examples: Throughput reads unavailable when nothing measured it; the gauge stays blank rather than guessing a number.
bad_examples: A cockpit that always shows a confident tokens-per-second figure, even when the runtime reported none.
